cohort: The study involved 66 mother-child pairs and 10 health workers across four primary healthcare centres in Imo state, Nigeria.
finding: The study identified several positive determinants (e.g., baby crying, education, support from midwives, health worker training and knowledge) and barriers (e.g., delayed milk flow, lack of knowledge, family influence, mother's health, cesarean section, lack of training/motivation) affecting the early initiation of breastfeeding from the perspective of mothers and health workers.
mod_finding: Delivery via cesarean section was identified as a barrier to the early initiation of breastfeeding.
